title: Near-convergent endpoint pairs cannot be realized by any prefix-expanding cyclic O/E path
statement: For a run-type leftover (L, o_min), the set A_{L,o} of cyclic O/E words with o_L = o_min, a0 >= 2, first isolated-OE r <= R(a0), and 3^{o_k} >= 2^k on every prefix is empty. In particular this kills L=25781 or an infinite near-convergent family.
counterexamples: The unique extremal path o_k = r(k) = min{r: 3^r >= 2^k} is a lattice path from (0,0) to (L, o_min) for every L >= 1. Every prefix satisfies 3^{o_k} >= 2^k by construction
The path starts OOE, so a0 = 2 and the first isolated-OE count is 0 = R(2). It is not a prefix OOEOE
On all 99 run-type leftovers at N0=10^6, including L=25781 (o=16266) and L=55293, A_{L,o} is nonempty. The ceiling Christoffel word of slope o_min/L is a second witness
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / prefix Diophantine order
notes: Prefix expansion plus a0 >= 2 is equivalent to the endpoint inequality 3^o > 2^L. A nonempty A_{L,o} is not an integer cycle. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: 99 run-type leftovers; spotlight L=25781 and L=55293; exact integer 2^k vs 3^{o_k}
